KEY MESSAGE 1... 
7:50 PM Update...
An MCS is ongoing and moving roughly east-southeast across
northern Indiana into Northwest Ohio this evening. The MCS has
maintained strength as moving east with SPC issuing a Severe
Thunderstorm Watch for the western half of the forecast area
through midnight tonight. Primary hazard will be damaging wind
gusts and a tornado or two. Can't rule out instances of heavy
rainfall with isolated flash flooding, particularly in urban and
well-saturated areas. 

Previous discussion...
Weak low pressure is located over NW Illinois with a warm front
extending east across northern Indiana into western Ohio. The 
warm front is identified primarily by a swath of dewpoints in 
the lower 70s that is advecting northward today. An MCS is 
ongoing across Lake Michigan this afternoon and a Severe 
Thunderstorm Watch extends as far east as Williams County Ohio 
through 7 PM. The northern portion of the MCS is expected to 
outpace the reservoir of unstable air and the associated 
moisture advection. The southern portion of the MCS is more 
likely to maintain strength into Indiana but unclear at this 
time the extent it can hold together into NW Ohio. The 
instability gradient is expected to lift north along the I-75 
corridor and possibly to the central highlands but only make 
slow progress to the northeast across Lake Erie tonight. CAMS 
have struggled with the handling of this MCS but best timing 
estimates are for a few thunderstorms to continue east along the
advancing warm front into the I-75 corridor and possibly 
towards Mansfield between 8-11 PM. A general weakening trend is 
likely as we get past sunset and uncertainty remains regarding 
the coverage of severe wind gusts into this evening. In general 
the timing of thunderstorms has trended faster into NW Ohio. 

Later tonight we expect to see a low level jet develop from Chicago 
into lower Michigan. This feature combined with the next round of 
shortwave energy moving through the quasi northwest flow aloft are 
likely to result in a rejuvenation of thunderstorms upstream across 
SW lower Michigan. Showers with scattered thunderstorms are expected 
to spread east across Lake Erie after midnight tonight while perhaps 
more robust convection still favors a southeast trajectory towards 
Central Ohio. Models over the last couple days have been 
highlighting a swath of heavier rain setting up just southwest of 
our forecast areas in Indiana/west central Ohio prior to 12Z.  

KEY MESSAGE 2...
The local area remains on the downstream side of an 
upper level ridge over the Rocky Mountains and Plains states through 
mid-week. This places the local area in a favorable region for 
additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms as the warm front 
stalls in the vicinity and multiple shortwaves move through the
flow aloft. Timing of additional showers and thunderstorms is 
challenging beyond tonight and will be impacted by storm 
evolution, outflow boundaries, and placement of the stalled 
front. We do expect a break during the late morning/early 
afternoon on Monday. Moderate instability is expected to 
develop through the afternoon, especially across southern 
portions of the forecast area, with scattered thunderstorms
possible during the late afternoon. A more organized severe 
weather threat could materialize during the evening ahead of a 
more substantial shortwave trough sliding through the Central 
Great Lakes. Good veering of the flow with height is expected 
along with around 40 knots of shear. Almost all of the forecast 
area is in a Slight Risk(level 2 of 5) for severe thunderstorms 
on Monday. 

Depending on storm evolution, a trailing rain threat could linger 
into Monday night, particularly closer to Central Ohio. With the 
potential for a stronger round of storms on Monday evening/night, 
did lower pops to chance for most of the daytime on Tuesday. 
The airmass remains very moist with PW values rebounding to near
2 inches but confidence in placement of storms is low by this 
time. The more active storm track could be just south of the 
area on Tuesday but will need to be monitored. Coverage is
likely to increase again Tuesday night. Then one more 
opportunity for thunderstorms is in the forecast on Wednesday 
afternoon ahead of the eventual cold front. Storm total rainfall
amounts through Wednesday are over 2 inches across southwest 
portions of the forecast area but could see localized totals of 
3 or more inches over several days. Will need to monitor the
potential for flooding as the week progresses and areas become
saturated. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...
